request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people, claims and pools exports now use the as-of figures while an as-of date is set. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What was wrong:** the people and claims exports were built in the browser from the data already on screen. Right after you set an as-of date, the screen is still reloading, so the people export came out empty (just the header row). The pools export didn't have this problem because it already re-read the data before building its file. Every read of a sheet sends the as-of date, so the server returns the figures as of that date.

**The fix** is all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The people and claims exports now re-read the sheet first, the same way the pools export does, so they always use the as-of figures. A small helper, `reloadForExport()`, does the re-read and skips the download if a different sheet was loaded in the meantime. I didn't need to change the server or the stored data.
